title: Backstabbed in a Backwater Dungeon: My Party Tried to Kill Me, But Thanks to an Infinite Gacha I Got LVL 9999 Friends and Am Out For Revenge
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Twelve-year-old Light, the only human in a multi-race adventuring party, is betrayed and left to die in the deepest dungeon. There his 'unlimited gacha' gift summons overwhelmingly powerful allies, led by the maid Mei. After finding his hometown massacred and humans enslaved by other races, he spends years building an underground base and sets out for revenge on his former party and on the races that oppress humanity.
life_message: Betrayal must be repaid in full, and power gathered from loyal followers is the way to set the world right.

content.note: Massacre of Light's village, enslavement and experiments on humans, and planned revenge on betrayers (Wikipedia premise; MU Torture, Slavery; AniList Revenge 90).
A child betrayed and left to die; slaughtered parents (Wikipedia).
Harem of 'sexy' summoned allies (Seven Seas blurb via MU); MU lists a Rape category (to verify); MangaDex suggestive.
Taunting of enemies ('zamaa') in the title (to verify).
Trauma and rage after betrayal; obsessive loyalty of allies (MU Obsessive Love).
Revenge and collective blame of whole races presented as justified (Wikipedia premise; AniList Revenge 90; MU Revenge).
Gacha game mechanic is the hero's power source (MU Gacha, Game Elements).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Betrayal must be avenged personally; the title promises 'zamaa' payback.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Light acts outside any law, building his own hidden power base.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to his own people, family and summoned retainers over the wider world.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Summoned allies serve Light as 'master' with total devotion.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Game-like ranks and gifts; no religious frame noted.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival and security of humans drive everything.

folkways.japan: The 'zamaa' (serves-you-right) revenge subgenre is a recognized web-novel trend in Japan, and loyal master-retainer devotion echoes older Japanese service ideals.

delivery.evidence: ANN anime preview: reviewers call the betrayers one-dimensional ('we're the baddies') and the revenge mean and contrived.

personified.ideology: betrayal must be repaid in full

delivery.note: The revenge motive is stated openly and the betrayers are drawn without a case of their own, per anime reviews.

winners_losers: Light and his loyal summons win; his betrayers and the races that enslave humans lose. Sympathy goes entirely to the avenger.
